[ASSISTANT_SAID] Snails can be indicators of environmental health as they are sensitive to changes in their environment.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Scientists use snails to monitor ecosystems by collecting and analyzing their shells, tissues, and feces to identify pollutants, toxins, or other environmental stressors.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Certain species of snails are used to monitor heavy metal contamination in water bodies.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Other species of snails are used to study the effects of pesticides on freshwater ecosystems.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The genetic diversity and community structure of snail populations can also be used to assess the health of an ecosystem.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Birds are used to monitor air and water quality as they can accumulate pollutants in their feathers, tissues, and eggs.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Fish are sensitive to changes in water quality and can show signs of stress or disease when conditions are not optimal.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Insects, such as bees and butterflies, are important pollinators and can indicate the health of ecosystems.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Amphibians, such as frogs and salamanders, are sensitive to changes in water quality and habitat loss.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Endangered animals can provide critical information about the health of their ecosystems.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Sea turtles are important indicators of the health of marine ecosystems.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Whales are important indicators of the health of ocean ecosystems.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Elephants are important indicators of the health of savanna and forest ecosystems.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The choice of using animal indicators or technology for monitoring ecosystems should be based on specific objectives and conditions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Animal-based monitoring may require more personnel, labor, and time for data collection and analysis.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Technology can provide precise measurements of environmental conditions in real-time.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Citizen science involves members of the public participating in scientific research projects.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] eBird is an online platform that allows birders to report sightings of birds and contribute to a growing database of avian biodiversity.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] iNaturalist is a mobile application that allows citizen scientists to record and share observations of plants and animals.
